normative.quote: This should not exclude the possibility of implementing TFTP on top of other datagram protocols.
normative.obligation: TFTP may be implemented over datagram protocols other than UDP.

normative.quote: The only thing it can do is read and write files (or mail) from/to a remote server. It cannot list directories
normative.obligation: An implementation offers only file read and write; no directory listing and no user authentication.

normative.quote: In common with other Internet protocols, it passes 8 bit bytes of data.
normative.obligation: Data is carried as 8-bit bytes.

normative.quote: Three modes of transfer are currently supported: netascii ... octet ... mail
normative.obligation: Exactly three transfer modes are defined by the protocol: netascii, octet, mail.

normative.quote: netascii (This is ascii as defined in "USA Standard Code for Information Interchange" [1] with the modifications specified in "Telnet Protocol Specification" [3].)
normative.obligation: netascii means 8-bit ASCII per USAS X3.4-1968 with the Telnet Protocol Specification modifications.

normative.quote: octet (This replaces the "binary" mode of previous versions of this document.) raw 8 bit bytes
normative.obligation: octet mode transfers raw 8-bit bytes and supersedes the former binary mode.

normative.quote: (The mail mode is obsolete and should not be implemented or used.)
normative.obligation: An implementation should not implement or use mail mode.

normative.quote: Additional modes can be defined by pairs of cooperating hosts.
normative.obligation: Modes beyond the three defined ones may be agreed bilaterally between cooperating hosts.

normative.quote: Reference [4] (section 4.2) should be consulted for further valuable directives and suggestions on TFTP.
normative.obligation: An implementation should also apply the directives of RFC 1123 section 4.2.

normative.quote: Any transfer begins with a request to read or write a file, which also serves to request a connection.
normative.obligation: Every transfer starts with a read or write request that simultaneously opens the connection.

normative.quote: If the server grants the request, the connection is opened and the file is sent in fixed length blocks of 512 bytes.
normative.obligation: On a granted request the file is transferred in fixed-length 512-byte blocks.

normative.quote: Each data packet contains one block of data
normative.obligation: A DATA packet carries exactly one block.

normative.quote: must be acknowledged by an acknowledgment packet before the next packet can be sent
normative.obligation: The sender must receive the ACK for a DATA packet before sending the next one (lock step).

normative.quote: A data packet of less than 512 bytes signals termination of a transfer.
normative.obligation: A DATA packet shorter than 512 bytes signals the end of the transfer.

normative.quote: If a packet gets lost in the network, the intended recipient will timeout
normative.obligation: A host times out when an expected packet does not arrive.

normative.quote: may retransmit his last packet (which may be data or an acknowledgment), thus causing the sender of the lost packet to retransmit
normative.obligation: On timeout a host may retransmit its own last packet, which prompts the peer to retransmit the lost one.

normative.quote: The sender has to keep just one packet on hand for retransmission
normative.obligation: A host retains exactly one packet (its last) for retransmission.

normative.quote: One sends data and receives acknowledgments, the other sends acknowledgments and receives data.
normative.obligation: Each transfer has two complementary roles: DATA sender/ACK receiver and ACK sender/DATA receiver.

normative.quote: Most errors cause termination of the connection.
normative.obligation: An error terminates the connection except for the one condition named later.

normative.quote: An error is signalled by sending an error packet.
normative.obligation: An implementation signals an error by sending an ERROR packet.

normative.quote: This packet is not acknowledged, and not retransmitted
normative.obligation: ERROR packets are never acknowledged and never retransmitted.

normative.quote: (i.e., a TFTP server or user may terminate after sending an error message)
normative.obligation: A host may terminate immediately after sending an ERROR packet.

normative.quote: Therefore timeouts are used to detect such a termination when the error packet has been lost.
normative.obligation: An implementation uses timeouts to detect a peer termination whose ERROR packet was lost.

normative.quote: not being able to satisfy the request (e.g., file not found, access violation, or no such user)
normative.obligation: Inability to satisfy a request is an error condition that raises an ERROR packet.

normative.quote: receiving a packet which cannot be explained by a delay or duplication in the network (e.g., an incorrectly formed packet)
normative.obligation: Receiving a packet not explainable as delay or duplication is an error condition.

normative.quote: losing access to a necessary resource (e.g., disk full or access denied during a transfer)
normative.obligation: Losing access to a needed resource mid-transfer is an error condition.

normative.quote: TFTP recognizes only one error condition that does not cause termination, the source port of a received packet being incorrect.
normative.obligation: An incorrect source port is the only error that does not terminate the connection.

normative.quote: In this case, an error packet is sent to the originating host.
normative.obligation: On a wrong-source-port packet, send an ERROR packet to the host that originated it.

normative.quote: the order of the contents of a packet will be: local medium header, if used, Internet header, Datagram header, TFTP header
normative.obligation: Headers appear in the order local medium, Internet, Datagram, TFTP, then the TFTP packet body.

normative.quote: |  Local Medium  |  Internet  |  Datagram  |  TFTP  |
normative.obligation: The figure fixes the header stacking order for a TFTP packet.

normative.quote: the source and destination port fields of the Datagram header ... are used by TFTP
normative.obligation: TFTP uses the datagram source and destination port fields.

normative.quote: the length field reflects the size of the TFTP packet
normative.obligation: The datagram length field reflects the size of the enclosed TFTP packet.

normative.quote: The transfer identifiers (TID's) used by TFTP are passed to the Datagram layer to be used as ports
normative.obligation: An implementation passes its TIDs to the datagram layer to serve as ports.

normative.quote: therefore they must be between 0 and 65,535
normative.obligation: A TID must be in the range 0 to 65535.

normative.quote: The  TFTP header consists of a 2 byte opcode field which indicates the packet's type
normative.obligation: Every TFTP packet begins with a 2-byte opcode field identifying its type.

normative.quote: A transfer is established by sending a request (WRQ to write onto a foreign file system, or RRQ to read from it)
normative.obligation: A transfer is initiated by sending WRQ (write) or RRQ (read).

normative.quote: receiving a positive reply, an acknowledgment packet for write, or the first data packet for read
normative.obligation: The positive reply is an ACK for a write request and the first DATA packet for a read request.

normative.quote: In general an acknowledgment packet will contain the block number of the data packet being acknowledged.
normative.obligation: An ACK carries the block number of the DATA packet it acknowledges.

normative.quote: Each data packet has associated with it a block number; block numbers are consecutive and begin with one.
normative.obligation: DATA block numbers start at one and run consecutively.

normative.quote: Since the positive response to a write request is an acknowledgment packet, in this special case the block number will be zero.
normative.obligation: The ACK that accepts a WRQ carries block number zero.

normative.quote: If the reply is an error packet, then the request has been denied.
normative.obligation: An ERROR packet in reply to a request means the request was denied.

normative.quote: each end of the connection chooses a TID for itself, to be used for the duration of that connection
normative.obligation: Each endpoint picks its own TID and keeps it for the whole connection.

normative.quote: The TID's chosen for a connection should be randomly chosen, so that the probability that the same number is chosen twice ... is very low
normative.obligation: TIDs should be chosen randomly so immediate reuse is improbable.

normative.quote: Every packet has associated with it the two TID's of the ends of the connection, the source TID and the destination TID.
normative.obligation: Every packet carries both the source TID and the destination TID.

normative.quote: These TID's are handed to the supporting UDP (or other datagram protocol) as the source and destination ports.
normative.obligation: TIDs are conveyed as the transport source and destination ports.

normative.quote: sends its initial request to the known TID 69 decimal (105 octal) on the serving host
normative.obligation: The client sends its initial RRQ/WRQ to destination TID 69 on the server.

normative.quote: uses a TID chosen by the server as its source TID and the TID chosen for the previous message by the requestor
normative.obligation: The server answers from a freshly chosen source TID addressed to the requestor's TID.

normative.quote: The two chosen TID's are then used for the remainder of the transfer.
normative.obligation: The negotiated TID pair is used unchanged for the rest of the transfer.

normative.quote: the first data packet can be sent by Host A with a sequence number of 1
normative.obligation: Once the connection is established the first DATA packet carries block number 1.

normative.quote: in all succeeding steps, the hosts should make sure that the source TID matches the value that was agreed on in steps 1 and 2
normative.obligation: Each host should check the source TID of every received packet against the agreed value.

normative.quote: If a source TID does not match, the packet should be discarded as erroneously sent from somewhere else.
normative.obligation: A packet with a non-matching source TID should be discarded.

normative.quote: An error packet should be sent to the source of the incorrect packet, while not disturbing the transfer.
normative.obligation: Send an ERROR packet to the source of a wrong-TID packet without disturbing the ongoing transfer.

normative.quote: When the second response to the request arrives, it should be rejected, but there is no reason to terminate the first connection.
normative.obligation: A second (duplicate-request) response is rejected while the first connection continues.

normative.quote: 1 Read request (RRQ) 2 Write request (WRQ) 3 Data (DATA) 4 Acknowledgment (ACK) 5 Error (ERROR)
normative.obligation: There are five packet types with opcode values 1 through 5 as listed.

normative.quote: The TFTP header of a packet contains the  opcode  associated  with that packet.
normative.obligation: The opcode in the header identifies the packet's type.

normative.quote: 2 bytes     string    1 byte     string   1 byte | Opcode |  Filename  |   0  |    Mode    |   0  |
normative.obligation: RRQ/WRQ layout is a 2-byte opcode, a filename string, a zero byte, a mode string, a zero byte.

normative.quote: RRQ and WRQ packets (opcodes 1 and 2 respectively) have the format shown in Figure 5-1.
normative.obligation: RRQ uses opcode 1, WRQ opcode 2, both in the Figure 5-1 format.

normative.quote: The file name is a sequence of bytes in netascii terminated by a zero byte.
normative.obligation: The filename field is netascii bytes terminated by a zero byte.

normative.quote: The mode field contains the string "netascii", "octet", or "mail" (or any combination of upper and lower case ...) in netascii
normative.obligation: The mode field holds one of the three mode names in netascii, matched case-insensitively.

normative.quote: A host which receives netascii mode data must translate the data to its own format.
normative.obligation: A receiver of netascii-mode data must convert it into its own local format.

normative.quote: Octet mode is used to transfer a file that is in the 8-bit format of the machine from which the file is being transferred.
normative.obligation: Octet mode carries the sending machine's 8-bit file format without translation.

normative.quote: If a host receives a octet file and then returns it, the returned file must be identical to the original.
normative.obligation: An octet-mode round trip must return a file byte-identical to the original.

normative.quote: It is also possible to define other modes for cooperating pairs of hosts ... There is no requirement that any other hosts implement these.
normative.obligation: Private modes may be defined between cooperating hosts, with no obligation on any other host.

normative.quote: 2 bytes     2 bytes      n bytes | Opcode |   Block #  |   Data     |
normative.obligation: DATA layout is a 2-byte opcode, a 2-byte block number, then n data bytes.

normative.quote: DATA packets (opcode = 3) have a block number and data field.
normative.obligation: DATA uses opcode 3 and carries a block number and a data field.

normative.quote: The block numbers on data packets begin with one and increase by one for each new block of data.
normative.obligation: Each new DATA block increments the block number by one, starting at one.

normative.quote: The data field is from zero to 512 bytes long.
normative.obligation: The DATA data field is between 0 and 512 bytes.

normative.quote: If it is 512 bytes long, the block is not the last block of data
normative.obligation: A 512-byte data field means more blocks follow; 0-511 bytes ends the transfer.

normative.quote: All  packets other than duplicate ACK's and those used for termination are acknowledged unless a timeout occurs [4].
normative.obligation: Every packet is acknowledged except duplicate ACKs and termination packets, absent a timeout.

normative.quote: Sending a DATA packet is an acknowledgment for the first ACK packet of the previous DATA packet.
normative.obligation: Sending the next DATA implicitly acknowledges the first ACK of the previous DATA.

normative.quote: The WRQ and DATA packets are acknowledged by ACK or ERROR packets, while RRQ and ACK packets are acknowledged by  DATA  or ERROR packets.
normative.obligation: WRQ and DATA are answered by ACK or ERROR; RRQ and ACK are answered by DATA or ERROR.

normative.quote: 2 bytes     2 bytes | Opcode |   Block #  |
normative.obligation: ACK layout is a 2-byte opcode followed by a 2-byte block number.

normative.quote: Figure 5-3 depicts an ACK packet; the opcode is 4.
normative.obligation: ACK uses opcode 4.

normative.quote: The  block  number  in an  ACK echoes the block number of the DATA packet being acknowledged.
normative.obligation: An ACK echoes the block number of the DATA packet it acknowledges.

normative.quote: A WRQ is acknowledged with an ACK packet having a block number of zero.
normative.obligation: A WRQ is acknowledged by an ACK with block number zero.

normative.quote: 2 bytes     2 bytes      string    1 byte | Opcode |  ErrorCode |   ErrMsg   |   0  |
normative.obligation: ERROR layout is a 2-byte opcode, 2-byte error code, error message string, zero byte.

normative.quote: An ERROR packet (opcode 5) takes the form depicted in Figure 5-4.
normative.obligation: ERROR uses opcode 5 in the Figure 5-4 format.

normative.quote: An ERROR packet can be the acknowledgment of any other type of packet.
normative.obligation: An ERROR packet may serve as the response to any packet type.

normative.quote: The error code is an integer indicating the nature of the error. A table of values and meanings is given in the appendix.
normative.obligation: The ErrorCode field is an integer drawn from the appendix table of error meanings.

normative.quote: The error message is intended for human consumption, and should be in netascii.
normative.obligation: The ErrMsg field should be human-readable netascii text.

normative.quote: Like all other strings, it is terminated with a zero byte.
normative.obligation: ErrMsg, like every TFTP string field, ends with a zero byte.

normative.quote: The end of a transfer is marked by a DATA packet that contains between 0 and 511 bytes of data (i.e., Datagram length < 516).
normative.obligation: The final DATA packet carries 0 to 511 data bytes, giving a datagram shorter than 516 bytes.

normative.quote: This packet is acknowledged by an ACK packet like all other DATA packets.
normative.obligation: The final DATA packet is acknowledged with an ACK like any other DATA packet.

normative.quote: The host acknowledging the final DATA packet may terminate its side of the connection on sending the final ACK.
normative.obligation: The acknowledger may close its side of the connection once it has sent the final ACK.

normative.quote: dallying is encouraged.  This means that the host sending the final ACK will wait for a while before terminating
normative.obligation: The host sending the final ACK is encouraged to dally so it can retransmit that ACK if lost.

normative.quote: The acknowledger will know that the ACK has been lost if it receives the final DATA packet again.
normative.obligation: Receiving the final DATA again tells the acknowledger its final ACK was lost.

normative.quote: The host sending the last DATA must retransmit it until the packet is acknowledged or the sending host times out.
normative.obligation: The sender must keep retransmitting the last DATA packet until it is acknowledged or it times out.

normative.quote: If the response is an ACK, the transmission was completed successfully.
normative.obligation: An ACK of the final DATA packet means the transfer completed successfully.

normative.quote: In any case, the connection has been closed.
normative.obligation: After the sender gives up retransmitting the final DATA, the connection is closed.

normative.quote: If a request can not be granted, or some error occurs during the transfer, then an ERROR packet (opcode 5) is sent.
normative.obligation: Send an ERROR packet when a request cannot be granted or an error occurs mid-transfer.

normative.quote: This is only a courtesy since it will not be retransmitted or acknowledged, so it may never be received.
normative.obligation: An ERROR packet is sent once, never retransmitted and never acknowledged.

normative.quote: Timeouts must also be used to detect errors.
normative.obligation: An implementation must use timeouts to detect errors.

normative.quote: 2 bytes ... |  Local Medium  |  Internet  |  Datagram  |  TFTP Opcode  |
normative.obligation: The 2-byte TFTP opcode follows the datagram header in the header stack.
The appendix restates the four wire formats with opcode numbers 01/02, 03, 04, 05 and field widths.

normative.quote: 0         Not defined, see error message (if any).
normative.obligation: Error code 0 means undefined; the meaning is carried by the error message.

normative.quote: 1         File not found.
normative.obligation: Error code 1 means the requested file was not found.

normative.quote: 2         Access violation.
normative.obligation: Error code 2 means an access violation.

normative.quote: 3         Disk full or allocation exceeded.
normative.obligation: Error code 3 means disk full or allocation exceeded.

normative.quote: 4         Illegal TFTP operation.
normative.obligation: Error code 4 means an illegal TFTP operation, such as a malformed or unexpected packet.

normative.quote: 5         Unknown transfer ID.
normative.obligation: Error code 5 means the packet carried an unknown transfer ID.

normative.quote: 6         File already exists.
normative.obligation: Error code 6 means the file already exists.

normative.quote: 7         No such user.
normative.obligation: Error code 7 means no such user.

normative.section: I. Appendix / Internet User Datagram Header
normative.quote: TFTP need not be implemented on top of the Internet User Datagram Protocol.
normative.obligation: UDP is not a mandatory transport for a TFTP implementation.

normative.quote: Source Port     Picked by originator of packet.
normative.obligation: The source port of each packet is the TID picked by the packet's originator.

normative.quote: Dest. Port      Picked by destination machine (69 for RRQ or WRQ).
normative.obligation: The destination port is the peer's chosen TID, and 69 for an initial RRQ or WRQ.

normative.quote: Length          Number of bytes in UDP packet, including UDP header.
normative.obligation: The datagram length counts the whole UDP packet including its 8-byte header (cf. RFC 1123 4.2.2.2).

normative.quote: (The implementor of this should be sure that the correct algorithm is used here.) Field contains zero if unused.
normative.obligation: The implementor should compute the datagram checksum with the correct algorithm, or send zero when unused.

normative.quote: TFTP passes transfer identifiers (TID's) to the Internet User Datagram protocol to be used as the source and destination ports.
normative.obligation: TIDs are handed to the datagram layer as the source and destination ports.

normative.quote: care must be taken in the rights granted to a TFTP server process so as not to violate the security
normative.obligation: A TFTP server process must be granted only file-system rights that do not compromise host security.

normative.quote: Vendors are urged to support TFTP for booting.
normative.obligation: A host implementation is urged to support TFTP for network bootstrapping.

normative.quote: The transfer mode "mail" SHOULD NOT be supported.
normative.obligation: An implementation should not support the mail transfer mode (amends RFC 1350 mail-mode text).

normative.quote: The Length field of a UDP header is incorrectly defined; it includes the UDP header length (8).
normative.obligation: The UDP Length field includes the 8-byte UDP header, correcting the base specification.

normative.quote: Implementations MUST contain the fix for this problem: the sender ... must never resend the current DATA packet on receipt of a duplicate ACK.
normative.obligation: The DATA sender must never retransmit the current DATA packet in response to a duplicate ACK (spans a page break).

normative.quote: A TFTP implementation MUST use an adaptive timeout.
normative.obligation: Retransmission timeouts must be adaptive rather than fixed.

normative.quote: A variety of non-standard extensions have been made to TFTP ... None of these have been standardized.
normative.obligation: TFTP extensions are non-standard and optional; an implementation need not support any of them.

normative.quote: A server TFTP implementation SHOULD include some configurable access control over what pathnames are allowed in TFTP operations.
normative.obligation: A server should provide configurable access control over the pathnames it will serve.

normative.quote: A TFTP request directed to a broadcast address SHOULD be silently ignored.
normative.obligation: A request received on a broadcast address should be dropped without any reply.

normative.quote: Fix Sorcerer's Apprentice Syndrome               |4.2.3.1 |x| | | | |
normative.obligation: The requirements summary rates the Sorcerer's Apprentice fix as MUST.

normative.quote: netascii                                       |RFC-783 |x| | | | |
normative.obligation: netascii transfer mode must be supported.

normative.quote: octet                                          |RFC-783 |x| | | | |
normative.obligation: octet transfer mode must be supported.
The summary rates mail mode as SHOULD NOT be supported.

normative.quote: extensions                                     |4.2.3.3 | | |x| | |
normative.obligation: Non-standard extensions may be supported at the implementer's option.

normative.quote: Use adaptive timeout                             |4.2.3.2 |x| | | | |
normative.obligation: The summary rates the adaptive timeout as MUST.

normative.quote: Configurable access control                      |4.2.3.4 | |x| | | |
normative.obligation: The summary rates configurable access control as SHOULD.

normative.quote: Silently ignore broadcast request                |4.2.3.5 | |x| | | |
normative.obligation: The summary rates silently ignoring broadcast requests as SHOULD.
